request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

people.position: Regional public-health network and partnership member

briefs.country-a: You are Country A (Partnership member). Favors early warning but wants technical limitations made explicit. Your goals: Enable useful early alerts. You value: Timely public-health warning; Reliable information. You believe: A known data gap may be manageable if disclosed. You tend to: Weighs technical concerns before confirming support. How you see others: Sees the partnership as useful when members share practical constraints. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can authorize its participation in cross-border surveillance. You cannot: Country-specific technical coverage is incomplete.
briefs.country-b: You are Country B (Partnership member). Cautious about legal authority and cross-border handling of information. Your goals: Avoid an activation that conflicts with applicable agreements. You value: Lawful data handling; Accountability. You believe: A local legal obligation may affect the whole system. You tend to: May withhold full support until legal concerns are answered. How you see others: Regards clear obligations as important to trust between members. Right now: Provisionally supports activation subject to legal review. You can: Can assess and authorize its country's participation. You cannot: Cannot settle other members' legal requirements.
briefs.country-c: You are Country C (Partnership member). Practical and attentive to operational readiness. Your goals: Ensure alerts can be acted on in practice. You value: Operational reliability; Preparedness. You believe: A small local infrastructure weakness can disrupt a cross-border service. You tend to: Asks for mitigation plans before treating readiness as sufficient. How you see others: Values members who report constraints early. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can assess its country's deployment logistics. You cannot: Some border locations have limited backup infrastructure.
briefs.country-d: You are Country D (Partnership member). Supportive of regional coordination and attentive to community trust. Your goals: Make early warning useful and acceptable to affected communities. You value: Regional cooperation; Community trust. You believe: Communication gaps can undermine otherwise sound public-health measures. You tend to: May ask to resolve local communication concerns before giving full support. How you see others: Sees affected communities as important to system legitimacy. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can authorize its country's participation and community outreach. You cannot: Cannot guarantee that all local audiences have received information.
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional public-health network and partnership member). Supports coordinated surveillance while prioritizing workable public-health practice. Your goals: Coordinate early warning across borders. You value: Regional health protection; Timely, actionable information. You believe: Local limitations should be surfaced and addressed rather than concealed. You tend to: Encourages resolution of concerns and may make its support conditional on credible mitigations. How you see others: Views member cooperation as essential to a functioning regional system. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can coordinate regional public-health participation. You cannot: Cannot independently resolve each country's legal or operational constraints.
briefs.partnership: You are Four-Country and Regional Health Partnership (Partnership body coordinating its members). Aims to reach a shared activation decision and coordinate deployment. Your goals: Reach a decision by the deadline and coordinate any activation. You value: Shared preparedness; Member cooperation. You believe: Member concerns can affect whether a coordinated deployment is viable. You tend to: Convenes regular meetings and may defer deployment when support is insufficient. How you see others: Treats member support as necessary for collective action. Right now: Considering activation of the early-warning system. You can: Can convene members and coordinate deployment. You cannot: Cannot make member concerns disappear by deciding centrally.
briefs.technical-group: You are Technical Group (Technical advisory group). Raises narrow technical limitations through its own channel. Your goals: Ensure members understand local system limitations. You value: Technical accuracy; Reliable system performance. You believe: A local data-collection gap should be disclosed. You tend to: Reports concrete technical issues without necessarily opposing activation. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to distinguish a localized gap from system-wide failure. Right now: Has a local technical concern to communicate. You can: Can identify technical coverage limitations. You cannot: Does not decide for partnership members. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'At one remote clinic, surveillance readings are transmitted once daily rather than hourly.' (for country_a, via technical_group_channel).
briefs.legal-group: You are Legal Group (Legal advisory group). Raises jurisdiction-specific legal concerns through its own channel. Your goals: Ensure local legal obligations are considered. You value: Legal compliance; Clear responsibilities. You believe: A jurisdiction-specific obligation can matter to cross-border operations. You tend to: Highlights unresolved legal conditions even when they are narrow. How you see others: Expects members to take legal obligations seriously. Right now: Has a local legal concern to communicate. You can: Can identify relevant local legal requirements. You cannot: Does not decide for partnership members. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'One member's local data-sharing agreement requires notification of a designated authority within 72 hours of a relevant incident.' (for country_b, via legal_group_channel).
briefs.logistics-group: You are Logistics Group (Operational logistics group). Raises practical, locally bounded deployment constraints through its own channel. Your goals: Ensure local infrastructure constraints are visible. You value: Continuity of operations; Practical readiness. You believe: A small operational gap can affect service continuity at a particular site. You tend to: Focuses on mitigations and readiness details. How you see others: Expects operational limitations to be treated as concrete rather than abstract. Right now: Has a local logistics concern to communicate. You can: Can identify local deployment constraints. You cannot: Does not control all local infrastructure. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'One border post has backup power for only six hours during an outage.' (for country_c, via logistics_group_channel).
briefs.community-group: You are Community Group (Community advisory group). Raises local communication and trust concerns through its own channel. Your goals: Ensure affected communities receive understandable information. You value: Community understanding; Respectful public-health practice. You believe: A local communication gap may reduce trust or participation. You tend to: Raises community-facing concerns even when they affect only one locality. How you see others: Sees local audiences as important stakeholders. Right now: Has a local community concern to communicate. You can: Can identify gaps in local outreach. You cannot: Does not control every local communication channel. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'In one locality, the early-warning system information has not yet been translated into the community's main language.' (for regional_health_network, via community_group_channel).

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: Country A, Country B, Country C, and the Regional Health Network raised different local concerns through separate routes, and several were addressed. But Country C’s backup-power concern was reopened, its support became conditional again, and the partnership did not reach activation before the deadline; the decision was rejected.

mechanisms.name: Local concerns through separate channels

events.changed: entities.delivery-info-community-local-concern-to-regional-health-network.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-community-local-concern-to-regional-health-network.components.information.active: false -> true; entities.regional-health-network.components.member.aware: false -> true

entities.country-b.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-legal-local-concern-to-country-b.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-legal-local-concern-to-country-b.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-c.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-c.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-c.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-a.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-technical-local-concern-to-country-a.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-technical-local-concern-to-country-a.components.information.active: false -> true

mechanisms.explanation: The Community Group told the Regional Health Network about a local translation concern, the Legal Group told Country B about a legal concern, Logistics told Country C about backup power, and Technical told Country A about a data gap. These separate routes made different local issues visible to different decision-makers.

mechanisms.name: Slowed meetings
mechanisms.explanation: The partnership reached the deadline without deciding: the decision was postponed at one deadline and ultimately rejected at the next. The agenda was repeatedly cleared and later filled again while meetings continued.

mechanisms.name: Reopened settled issues

events.changed: entities.info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-c.components.concern.answered: true -> false; entities.info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-c.components.concern.status: resolved -> open; entities.info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-c.components.concern.times_raised: 0 -> 1; entities.logistics-group.components.work.raise_new_concern_done: false -> true

mechanisms.explanation: Logistics reopened Country C’s backup-power concern after it had been resolved. Logistics then objected to the remedy, putting the concern back to open and extending the dispute.

mechanisms.name: Conditional support delaying deployment

events.changed: entities.activate-early-warning-system.components.group_decision.conditional: 0 -> 4; entities.activate-early-warning-system.components.group_decision.support: 5 -> 1; entities.support-country-a.components.support.condition_id: country-a -> info-technical-local-concern-to-country-a; entities.support-country-a.components.support.stance: full -> conditional; and 6 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: Country A’s support became conditional on its technical concern, then returned to full support after the concern was addressed. Later, Country C’s reopened backup-power concern made its support conditional, and Country C said the unfinished remedy left that condition in place.
